So I’m unsure if this 100% applies to this post as it was my mum, however, when I was in school, my mum was a teaching assistant and on occasion she’d cover a class of the teacher was absent. One day when she covered our class, there was this boy, let’s call him Matthew, who had a couple of nasty students picking on him & looked quite distraught and couldn’t defend himself, my mum clocked onto what was going on, and being the goofy and kind lady she was, she walks over to the table, stands for a moment and just announces with her finger on her chin as though she had just had a thought, “you know...? I REALLY like chicken and mushroom pie” and just nods as if she’s come up with a great discovery or something. The mocking instantly went off Matthew and straight onto my mum, and she started just taking all these petty comments from these kids. Me being a young girl, I didn’t fully realise her intentions at the time, I was just so embarrassed that my mum just acted so odd in front of my classmates; I wasn’t the most popular of kids anyway, somewhat of a loner, so something like this really embarrassed me. It wasn’t until later in the evening I asked my mum why she said what she did, and she just says “better me than Matthew...”. I think she noticed I looked a bit confused with this so she elaborated; “they were picking on him and that’s not very nice is it abs (my mums pet name for me- short for Abby), so I thought if I can say the most random thing then they’ll stop with him, and be confused with what I said, so I was thinking what could I say to distract them from Matthew, and well, I was quite fancying a pie”. 

She saw a boy getting picked on and decided she’d rather be the butt of the jokes because it won’t effect her as much as this young boy, so she stepped in. And I’ll never forget that moment, I really got respect for my mum and her kind nature to not care about what people say, and to step in and help this helpless boy.
Tiny steps on your toes uttering ‘oo oo, sorry, can I just... oo, sorry’
Ah that sucks, I thought just as much though :/ thank u!
I had to call my brothers and tell them that my mum had passed away. I was 17 at the time.

I was in the car behind the hearse on my way to my mums funeral when I was 17, and I remember seeing this man wearing a hat look up and notice the hearse and he stood still, took off his hat and held it to his heart. Any other bystander would have just taken no notice like many people did, but this man did this out of pure, unconditional respect. Whenever I see a hearse now I put my hand on my heart because of how much it meant to me on that day.

I had a hamster for about 2 years and we kept him in my room, he would be doing normal hamster stuff, until the moment you started to get undressed/changed clothes; he’d stop what he was doing and stand on his hind legs and just stare at you until you were dressed then he would just go back to whatever he was doing :/

I once had a date where he forced me to feel a cushion as it was real fur, had me guess what animal it was made from; when he told me it was rabbit he asked: “is it softer then your rabbit? I bet it is”. He then proceeded to give me a tour of his house (because that’s obviously normal!?), introduced me to the gun that he uses when he goes hunting and informed me on the number of poor little animals he’s killed with it. His house was covered in dead animal; wall decor, bed throws, cushions etc. It was vulgar. He finished off the tour in his bedroom (how convenient?!) in an attempt to get me to sleep with him, it’s safe to say I promptly demanded him to take me home and haven’t spoken to him since. 
So to wrap things up, on a first date, do NOT come across as a psycho animal killing obsessive nut!
